body_markdown: The Petersen Automotive Museum is one of our favorite places to spend an afternoon. With ever-changing exhibits and a vast Vault to explore, there’s always something new to discover. The Petersen’s latest is located in the Armand Hammer Foundation Gallery on the museum’s ground floor, a spot typically reserved for[artistic displays](https://www.hagerty.com/media/events/l-a-s-petersen-museum-reunites-warhols-mercedes-commissions-with-their-muses/) such as this. *Flat Out* , a collection of work by Los Angeles’ own Joshua Vides, features several cars and car body panels given a stark black-and-white paint job that the museum describes as transforming “everyday objects and environments into high-contrast experiences that dissolve the distinction between reality and illustration.” [Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/) [Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/) The cars themselves would be worth noting even without their artistic metamorphosis. It’s not too often that you see a[DeTomaso Longchamp](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/de-tomaso-longchamp-italian-dream-cruiser/) or[Citroën SM](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/driving-citroens-infamously-complex-sm-is-pure-delight/) in Los Angeles. Seeing them in the context of the exhibit is another experience entirely, as Vides’ hand-drawn style offers a subtle but surreal attack on your senses. It’s like you’ve stepped into a 1980s music video or a car-centric manga. The effect works well on the various hoods on the wall, but in this exhibit, you can get into the scene and walk among the cars to experience the strange shift in perspective Vides facilitates. [Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/) [Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/) The Detomaso Longchamp was powered by a Ford 351 V-8. It’s a more angular version of its sister car, the Maserati Kyalami. [Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/) Vides said his artistic style takes physical objects and renders them backward as a “Reality to Idea.” These real cars have virtually returned to the drawings that sparked their development. It’s one of the more interesting exhibits we’ve seen at the Petersen and is best experienced in person. *Flat Out* will be on display until July 5, 2027. If you’re in the Los Angeles area and want to stop by, you can find tickets[here](https://petersen.org/pages/tickets) .
